steps.title: Fresh and peppery
steps.body: Grüner Veltliner, often just Grüner, gives whites with lemon, lime, green apple, pear, green bean, lentil and its signature white pepper. Acidity is medium to high. It ranges from light, crisp everyday wines to powerful, rich ones. It's Austria's most planted grape, about a third of its vineyards.

steps.title: Origins
steps.body: Grüner Veltliner is native to Austria. DNA shows its parents are Traminer and an old grape found in St. Georgen, near Lake Neusiedl, called St. Georgener-Rebe. Despite its name, it isn't related to Roter Veltliner. It's vigorous and productive, so yield control decides quality.

steps.prompt: What is Grüner Veltliner's signature aroma?
steps.explanation: A white pepper note sets it apart.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for pale lemon, sometimes green-tinged colour, citrus and green apple with white pepper and vegetal notes like green bean, and a crisp, fresh palate. Richer versions add stone fruit, spice and a creamy texture. Compared with Sauvignon Blanc, it's less pungent and more peppery.

steps.prompt: Grüner Veltliner is Austria's most planted grape.
steps.explanation: Yes, about a third of its vineyards.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Grüner gives citrus, green apple and white pepper
It's Austria's native and most planted grape
Its parents are Traminer and St. Georgener-Rebe
